{{Quote|War is a vile thing, and it brings out the worst in beings. But it also brings out their best&mdash;courage, sacrifice, resourcefulness, tenacity, comradeship, genius, even humor. Would that we could achieve that enlightened state without shedding blood first.|Peet Sieben|<ref name="TCWn" />}}
[[Jal Shey Mentor|Mentor]] '''Peet Sieben''' was a philosopher who lived during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]<ref name="TCWn" /> in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref name="ERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> Sieben was a member of the [[Jal Shey]], an ancient order of the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] dedicated to studying [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] as a solely intellectual endeavor. Sieben believed that war was a terrible thing but acknowledged that it brought out great qualities in people. However, Sieben wished conflict did not have to be such a critical catalyst for those traits to emerge.<ref name="TCWn" />

==Behind the scenes==
Sieben was mentioned in [[Karen Traviss]]'s [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (novelization)|novelization]] of the [[2008]] [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]].<ref name="TCWn" />
